statement: Square $ABCD$ has side length $6$, with its vertices labeled in order around the square. Inside the square, a quarter circle with center $A$ and radius $6$ is drawn from $B$ to $D$, and a quarter circle with center $B$ and radius $6$ is drawn from $A$ to $C$. What is the area of the part of the square that lies outside both quarter circles?

choices.misconception: I added up the covered region using only one of the two $30^\circ$ sectors next to the equilateral triangle, so I subtracted $3\pi + 9\sqrt{3}$ instead of $6\pi + 9\sqrt{3}$.
I found the area of the region inside both quarter circles and subtracted only that from the square.
I added up the two $30^\circ$ sectors for the covered region but forgot the equilateral triangle between them.
I found the area of the region inside both quarter circles instead of the region outside both of them.

hints: Let $P$ be the point where the two arcs cross. What kind of triangle is $ABP$?

$PA = PB = AB = 6$, so triangle $ABP$ is equilateral. The covered part of the square splits into triangle $ABP$, a sector at $A$ between $\overline{AP}$ and $\overline{AD}$, and a sector at $B$ between $\overline{BP}$ and $\overline{BC}$.

Each of those sectors has angle $90^\circ - 60^\circ = 30^\circ$, so its area is $\frac{30}{360} \cdot 36\pi = 3\pi$. The triangle has area $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \cdot 6^2 = 9\sqrt{3}$. Subtract the covered area from $36$.

solutions.reliable: Let the arcs cross at $P$. Then $PA = 6$ (on the arc centered at $A$) and $PB = 6$ (on the arc centered at $B$), so triangle $ABP$ is equilateral and $\angle PAB = \angle PBA = 60^\circ$. The region of the square covered by at least one quarter circle is bounded by $\overline{AB}$, $\overline{BC}$, the arc from $C$ to $P$, the arc from $P$ to $D$, and $\overline{DA}$. It splits into three pieces: triangle $ABP$ with area $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \cdot 36 = 9\sqrt{3}$; the sector at $A$ between $\overline{AP}$ and $\overline{AD}$, with angle $90^\circ - 60^\circ = 30^\circ$ and area $\frac{30}{360} \cdot 36\pi = 3\pi$; and the matching sector at $B$, also $3\pi$. The covered area is $6\pi + 9\sqrt{3}$, so the uncovered area is $36 - 6\pi - 9\sqrt{3}$, which is about $1.56$.
solutions.elegant: Inclusion-exclusion gives the same total. Each quarter circle has area $9\pi$. The region inside both is two $60^\circ$ sectors (at $A$ and at $B$, each of area $6\pi$) overlapping in triangle $ABP$, so its area is $12\pi - 9\sqrt{3}$. The covered area is $9\pi + 9\pi - (12\pi - 9\sqrt{3}) = 6\pi + 9\sqrt{3}$, and the answer is $36 - 6\pi - 9\sqrt{3}$.
